## Summary
- Diagnostic Category: [`lint/nursery/noUselessFallbackInSpread`](/reference/diagnostics#diagnostic-category)
- This rule has an [**unsafe**](/linter/#unsafe-fixes) fix.
- The default severity of this rule is [**warning**](/reference/diagnostics#warning).
- Sources: 
  - Same as [`unicorn/no-useless-fallback-in-spread`](https://github.com/sindresorhus/eslint-plugin-unicorn/blob/main/docs/rules/no-useless-fallback-in-spread.md)

## How to configure
```json title="biome.json"
{
	"linter": {
		"rules": {
			"nursery": {
				"noUselessFallbackInSpread": "error"
			}
		}
	}
}

```
## Description
Disallow empty object fallbacks when spreading a value into an object.

Spreading `null`, `undefined`, or another falsy value (a value treated as `false` in a
condition, such as `false`, `0`, or `""`) into an object literal adds no properties.
Writing `{...(value || {})}` or `{...(value ?? {})}` therefore gives the same result as
`{...value}`, and the `{}` fallback only adds noise.

This doesn't apply to arrays: spreading `null` or `undefined` into an array or a function
call throws an error, so `[...(value || [])]` is allowed.

## Examples

### Invalid

```js
const object = { ...(options || {}) };
```

### Valid

```js
const object = { ...options };
const withDefaults = { ...(options || { verbose: true }) };
const conditional = { ...(enabled && {}) };
const array = [...(items || [])];
```
